sentences.text:
The essential details of the claim petition are as follows: On January 20, 2018, around 3:00 p.m.,
the deceased individual named Mehabubsab was riding his motorcycle with registration number KA-25/EG-1522.
He was en route to Varur village in the Hubballi taluka, with the purpose of engaging in tile fitting work.

Unfortunately, at that very moment near Cult Hotel, a Chassis Lorry with registration number TN-87/A-TMP- 6170, coming from Haveri towards Hubballi, recklessly and negligently disregarded traffic regulations.
This resulted in a collision between the Chassis Lorry and Mehabubsab's motorcycle, occurring from the rear end of the latter.
Tragically, the impact inflicted fatal injuries upon Mehabubsab.
He was promptly transported to KIMS Hospital in Hubballi, where he succumbed to his injuries on the same day.
Based on these events, the legal representatives of the deceased Mehabubsab have lodged a claim petition, seeking compensation for the aforementioned reasons.
In pursuance to the notice, respondent No.1 appeared in person and respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel.
Respondent No.1 has not filed any objection despite sufficient opportunity has been provided to him.

The substance of the statement of objections filed by the 2nd respondent is that the deceased was riding the motorcycle in the middle of road and he has taken turn towards right side and came in contact with the Chassis, as a result of which, the said accident had occurred.
There was contributory negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle.

The claim petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner of vehicle as well as insurer of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EG-1522 are proper and necessary parties to the claim petition.
Further, it is submitted that the driver of Chassis Lorry bearing No.TN-87/A- TMP-6170 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said lorry.
Further, he has denied the remaining allegations of the petition as false and sought for dismissal of the petition.

5. Based on the rival pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following issues :
NC: 2023:KHC-D:9131-DB "1. Whether the petitioners prove that 20.01.2018 at about 3.00 p.m. near Cult Hotel, Varur village, P.B.Road, Hubballi, when the deceased-Mehabubsab was going on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/EG-1522 at the same time one Lorry bearing registration No.TN-87/A-6170 came in high speed and rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed against the motorcycle, as a result deceased-Mehabubsab sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the accidental injuries?
2. Whether respondents prove that petition is not maintainable?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount with interest as sought for?

4. What order or award?"

sentences.text: In order to prove their case, only petitioner No.1 was examined as P.W.1, 13 documents were marked as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
Respondents have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.

However,
respondent No.2 produced a copy of insurance policy, which was marked as Ex.R.1.

On hearing the arguments, the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.18,25,000/- along with NC: 2023:KHC-D:9131-DB interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
7. Being aggrieved by the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal, the Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.

8. The learned counsel appearing for appellant-Insurance Company has submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has not noticed the fact that the driver of the insured vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The Tribunal has also not noticed the fact that the accident occurred in the middle of the road and the deceased should have taken the care while riding the motorcycle.

The accident occurred due to self negligence of the deceased, who was riding the motorcycle in the middle of the road, the panchanama supports the said aspect, which clearly shows that the accident had occurred in the middle of the road.
The deceased has also contributed to the accident.
Further, it is submitted that the Tribunal arbitrarily considered the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.12,000/- without any proof.
On all these grounds, sought for allowing of this appeal.
As against this, the learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1 to 3/claimants submits that the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law and facts.
He further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards loss of consortium as per the Judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court.
There are no grounds to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award and accordingly, sought for dismissal of this appeal.
10. Having heard the arguments on both sides, and on perusal of the material on record, the following points would arise for our consideration.
(1) Whether the appellant has made out grounds to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award as to the quantum of compensation as well as the liability on the Insurance Company?
(2) What order or award?

11. Our findings to the above points are as follows :
Point No.1 in the negative.
Point No.2 as per the final order

Upon thorough consideration of the presented material, it is evident that the appellant has not contested the occurrence of the accident.
The appellant's stance centers around asserting contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
However, the evidence derived from the prosecution documents furnished by the petitioners contradicts this claim.
The Investigating Officer, after a comprehensive inquiry, has submitted a charge sheet against the driver of the involved Chassis Lorry.

13. The respondents have refrained from challenging the oral and documentary evidence presented,
and have not disputed the rash and negligent conduct exhibited by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Remarkably, the respondents have not provided any evidence to undermine the credibility of the oral and documentary evidence provided by the petitioners.

Upon an assessment of the evidence, the Tribunal has appropriately determined that there are no legitimate grounds to conclude that the accident resulted from contributory negligence on the part of the motorcycle rider.
It has rightly determined that the accident is a direct result of the sole negligent action of the Chassis Lorry driver.
After re-evaluating the evidence available, there are no identified legal deficiencies or unlawful aspects in the Tribunal's findings concerning the rash and negligent behavior of the Lorry's driver.
Consequently, the appellant-insurance company has not presented sufficient reasons to warrant intervention in this regard.
With regard to the quantum of compensation, the Insurance Company has not disputed the age of the deceased, multiplier adopted by the Tribunal.

But they have disputed as to the income of the deceased that the Tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.12,000/- per month without any proof and it is submitted that in view of the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the Tribunal ought to have assessed the notional income of deceased at the rate of Rs.11,750/- per month.

Considering the age and occupation of the deceased and also the evidence of P.W.1, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.11,000/- per month,
which is not on higher side.

Apart from this, the Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards loss of consortium as per the Judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court, firstly in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157 and - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:9131-DB secondly in the case of Magma General Insurance company Limited vs.
Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others, reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium only to the 1st petitioner.
Viewed from any angle, we do not find any illegalities or infirmities in the impugned Judgment and Award as to the quantum of compensation.
Hence, we answer point No.1 in the negative.

15. For the aforesaid discussions, we proceed to pass the following :
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
